The Nurse Manager for Acute Care at the James A. Haley Veterans' Hospital & Clinics is a frontline supervisory leader responsible for 24/7 oversight of assigned inpatient units, ensuring high-quality, Veteran-centered care.

The Nurse Manager provides clinical and administrative leadership, drives evidence-based practice, and fosters a culture of safety, engagement, and accountability. This role requires strong communication, team-building skills, and the ability to collaborate across interdisciplinary teams to achieve optimal Veteran outcomes.

Responsibilities include staff oversight, resource allocation, performance management, and participation in organizational initiatives to support nursing excellence.

Major duties include, but are not limited to: - Provides leadership, supervision, and 24/7 oversight for assigned Acute Care units including ICU, Progressive Care, STAT Team, Inpatient Case Management, Med-Surg Units, and Centralized Telemetry, with authority for both clinical and administrative operations. - Coordinates and evaluates patient care delivery using the full nursing process, ensuring high-quality, age-appropriate, Veteran-centered care. - Oversees staffing, develops schedules, validates data, and participates in staffing methodology processes. - Leads recruitment efforts, conducts interviews, and selects qualified candidates in coordination with the Nurse Recruiter. - Provides orientation, training, and ongoing competency development for staff; evaluates performance through proficiencies and appraisals. - Supports and drives evidence-based practice, quality improvement, and nurse-sensitive indicator performance, including data collection, analysis, trending, and reporting.- Ensures compliance with all accreditation and regulatory standards and maintains continual survey readiness. - Collaborates with interdisciplinary teams to remove barriers, enhance care processes, and implement innovative programs that improve Veteran outcomes. - Promotes an inclusive, culturally competent, and psychologically safe work environment aligned with organizational values, ethics, and EEO principles. - Participates in shared governance councils, organizational strategic planning, and the development of care delivery models. - Serves as a role model and servant leader, maintaining open communication with staff, peers, and union partners; conducts regular staff meetings with union invitations. - May provide cross-coverage within Acute Care and may be required to travel between hospital and clinic sites as needed.

The primary responsibility of the Registered Nurse - Survivorship Care Coordinator is to coordinate the journey of the veteran patient with cancer through the health care system. The incumbent of this position is essential to the successful operation and outcomes of the cancer treatments received in the Hematology/Oncology Department.

The incumbents' activities are dedicated to the timely access to quality care and treatment for patients with cancer which increases patient safety and satisfaction. The nurse is a stable and reliable point of contact for Veteran patients, providers, and member of the clinical team.

The incumbent provides oversight of the patient's journey through the diagnostic and treatment continuum, ensuring that all steps in the process are scheduled, and completed timely.

Incumbent is responsible for tracking the overall treatment plan while following select patients from the earliest suspicion of cancer through the continuum of cancer care inclusive of diagnosis, treatment, survivorship/surveillance and or palliation/end of life.

Typical procedures include PET scanning or other designated Nuclear Medicine procedures, radiology or laboratory studies; pre-operative diagnostic studies coordinated with clinical subspecialties such as Surgery, Cardiology or Dental Service; and /or facilitating clinic appointments, coordination and arranging diagnostic endoscopies or other invasive procedures.

Preferred Experience: - Experience with clinical software and EHR systems (Epic, Cerner, Meditech), including configuration, testing, and evaluating system effectiveness. - Ability to advise leadership on EHR functionality and participate in system development and reporting. - Background in multiple nursing specialties (e.g., PCU, Med/Surg, ED, ICU, OR, PACU, L&D). - Experience in clinical informatics, application programming, or health information systems supporting multidisciplinary care. - Proven participation in software implementation projects across departments. - Experience creating and delivering EHR training for clinical and non-clinical staff. - Knowledge of change-management strategies to support staff through system transitions. - Skill in workflow analysis and process redesign to improve efficiency and patient safety. - Experience assisting with planning, implementation, and troubleshooting of clinical software. - Strong communication skills with the ability to liaise between clinical users and IT teams Physical Requirements: This Position includes a level of physicality normally associated with duties performed by nurses such as direct patient care, and potentially long periods of walking, standing, sitting, moderate lifting, repeated bending, or kneeling.

The RN - Wound Care is a professional nurse (RN) with extensive clinical and technical knowledge in wound care. This person is responsible to assess, plan, evaluate, coordinate and establish the individualized care plan for all residents/patients with wound/ostomy needs.

The wound care RN is certified and their scope includes inpatient areas, outpatient areas and the CLC. Provide and assess variety of wounds, including pressure ulcers, and arterial, venous, diabetic, traumatic, burns and skin tears. Complete wound assessment including picture taking and downloading to CPRS.

Educate nursing staff about pressure ulcer staging, wound descriptions and partial and full thickness wounds. Educate nursing staff, veterans and significant others about wound and ostomy care. Complete negative pressure wound therapy and complete dressing changes. Provide care and education in acute care, ICU, CLC and outpatient clinic setting.

Participate in new employee orientation and educate visiting nursing and dietary students. Provide ostomy care and education pre and post-operative. This includes stoma measuring, assisting with the correct pouching system.

Educating veteran and care givers in regards to stoma care and applying wafer/ pouch, as well as troubleshooting a stomal/peri-stomal complications that may arise. Collaborate with surgery and primary care physicians to provide and plan of care. Collaborate with physicians to provide continuity of care.

Collaborate with Community Health Nursing staff and Home Health agencies to provide the best care for our Veterans out in the community. Manage Wound care RN outpatient wound care clinic, scheduling, recommend treatments, and work with other disciplines including Primary care physicians, surgery staff, and community health nurse.

Dipl. Pflegefachfrau/mann FH 80-100% Bruderholz gesucht – Werde Teil eines professionellen Teams
Bruderholz liegt in der Region Basel-Landschaft und bietet eine hervorragende Verkehrsanbindung durch direkte Zugverbindungen sowie gute Straßenanbindungen. Die Nähe zu Basel macht die Region als Arbeitsort besonders attraktiv für Sie, da Sie von kurzen Pendeldistanzen und einer gut ausgebauten Infrastruktur profitieren. Das Gebiet besticht durch seine grüne Umgebung und das gute Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis bei gleichzeitiger Nähe zu urbanen Zentren.
**Einsatzort:** Bruderholz und Umgebung
**Einsatzbeginn:** Ab sofort oder nach Vereinbarung
